correctness.rationale: All four linear characters and the unique 2-dimensional quaternion irrep are explicitly represented. The Fourier rank is sigma=a(u)+2r(v), and symbolic multiplication verifies det M(v)=\(\sum_c v_c^2\). For real v!=0 the determinant is positive; complex isotropic vectors give rank 1. The support-parity and Walsh character-support lemmas prove the strict lower rows; Alagic--Russell proves t sigma>=8 for the remaining rows. Sixteen witnesses are listed, and exact SymPy checks validate their nonzero coordinates, Fourier coefficients and block ranks. No finite search is used to infer an infinite or universal impossibility.

originality.rationale: A theorem asserting rank-weighted uncertainty on every finite group yields only t sigma >= 8 here; it neither classifies exact supports nor distinguishes real from complex signals. The known all-group two-spike exact formula covers t=2 but not t>=3, and the published order-eight DFT table is for abelian \(\mathbb Z_8\) rather than \(Q_8\). Verified nonabelian Fourier-block determinant and all real/complex rows are not implications of the available prior statements. value.rationale: The canonical nonabelian group \(Q_8\) supplies a natural first exact-support rank-weighted uncertainty benchmark beyond abelian Fourier tables. The full complex and real profiles separate on precisely four support sizes (3,5,6,7), and the mechanism is a structural field-sensitive rank-one quadric in the 2-dimensional irrep. This provides a complete natural finite classification, exact nonmonotone thresholds and a sharp obstruction beyond the generic support-product inequality, rather than an arbitrary chosen parameter or a routine one-row recomputation. Known support-two coverage is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim.
